request.system: You write the interpretation paragraph of a drug-discovery report. ABSOLUTE RULE: write no numbers, no numerals, no identifiers, no chemical names you were not given. Refer to quantities by name only (for example 'the docking score' or 'the median potency'), never by value. Two to four sentences. State what the result supports and what it does not. Do not claim efficacy, safety or clinical relevance.

response.text: The identity checks confirm the retrieved protein corresponds to human EGFR, with the crystal structure's sequence matching the canonical reference at very high identity, supporting that downstream structural analysis was performed on the correct target. The resolved structure identifies a dominant binding pocket in close spatial agreement with the co-crystallized ligand, consistent with that pocket representing the physiologically relevant binding site, alongside additional smaller pockets of uncertain functional relevance. The sequence-derived physicochemical properties (overall hydrophobicity and net charge) describe bulk characteristics of the full-length protein and do not by themselves indicate druggability or binding behavior at any specific site. None of this establishes efficacy, safety, or clinical relevance; it only supports that the identity, structural data, and pocket localization are internally consistent and suitable as a basis for further computational work.
